input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I see on my phone that I have a strong signal and it says 5G at the top, but there’s a little icon that looks like mobile data is turned off. I’m not sure if I’m connected to Wi-Fi right now. I can make regular calls, but I don’t think I can use mobile data at the moment. What should I do next?
Okay, I turned on the mobile data like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else I should try?
I tried to check if I could use the internet with mobile data, but it doesn’t seem to be working—nothing loads. What should I do now?

I checked, and there’s no airplane icon at the top of my screen, so I don’t think Airplane Mode is on. My phone isn’t showing any messages about the SIM card either—it seems normal. What should I try next?

I looked at the APN settings, but I’m not really sure what I’m looking at. It says the APN name is “internet,” but I don’t see anything listed for the MMSC URL. Is that a problem? Should I reset something? I’m a bit confused.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. But now you’re saying I need to restart my phone? I’m a little nervous—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? I really don’t want to lose anything important.
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? Is there anything else we can try?
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Is there something else I should look at or try?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it already has access to storage, SMS, and phone. Is there anything else that could be causing this problem?
I checked, and my phone is already set to “4G/5G preferred” for the network mode. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.
Yes, I think that would be best. I’m feeling a bit lost with all these technical things, so if someone can look into it more closely, I’d really appreciate it. Thank you for your help so far.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem. First, I need to identify your account to check your service status and settings.

Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll be able to assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and use mobile data (like browsing the web) on your phone right now?
- Are you currently connected to Wi-Fi, or are you using mobile data?

This will help me determine the next steps to resolve your MMS issue.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I see on my phone that I have a strong signal and it says 5G at the top, but there’s a little icon that looks like mobile data is turned off. I’m not sure if I’m connected to Wi-Fi right now. I can make regular calls, but I don’t think I can use mobile data at the moment. What should I do next?

It sounds like your mobile data might be turned off, which is required for sending MMS (picture messages), even if you have a strong signal and can make calls.

Please turn on your mobile data in your phone’s settings. Once mobile data is enabled, try sending the picture message again.

If you’re not sure how to turn on mobile data, let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy), and I can guide you through the steps. After you’ve turned on mobile data, let me know if the MMS goes through or if you still have issues.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Okay, I turned on the mobile data like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else I should try?

Thank you for turning on mobile data. Since you’re still unable to send picture messages, let’s check a few more things to identify the issue.

Could you please check if you can browse the web or use any apps that require internet access (without Wi-Fi)? This will help confirm if your mobile data is working properly.

If you can’t access the internet, let me know. If you can, we’ll move on to checking your MMS settings.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to check if I could use the internet with mobile data, but it doesn’t seem to be working—nothing loads. What should I do now?

Since your mobile data isn’t working, that’s likely why MMS isn’t going through. Let’s troubleshoot your mobile data connection first.

To start, please check if Airplane Mode is turned off on your phone. You can usually see an airplane icon at the top of your screen if it’s on. If it’s on, please turn it off.

If Airplane Mode is already off, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Is your phone showing any messages about the SIM card (like “No SIM” or “SIM error”), or does it seem normal?

Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue from there.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your SIM card is active and working.

I checked, and there’s no airplane icon at the top of my screen, so I don’t think Airplane Mode is on. My phone isn’t showing any messages about the SIM card either—it seems normal. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking those details. Since Airplane Mode is off and your SIM card appears normal, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent mobile data and MMS from working.

Could you please check your APN settings on your phone? If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy), and I can guide you through the steps.

Once you’ve checked, let me know if you see anything unusual or if you need help resetting the APN settings. If you’re unsure, I can walk you through resetting them to default, which often resolves this type of issue.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I looked at the APN settings, but I’m not really sure what I’m looking at. It says the APN name is “internet,” but I don’t see anything listed for the MMSC URL. Is that a problem? Should I reset something? I’m a bit confused.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The missing MMSC URL is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages (MMS). Resetting your APN settings to default should restore the correct values, including the MMSC URL.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you’ll need to restart (reboot) your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions for resetting the APN settings and rebooting your phone? If so, please let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy), and I’ll guide you through the process.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. But now you’re saying I need to restart my phone? I’m a little nervous—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Rest assured, restarting (rebooting) your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. It simply turns your phone off and back on to refresh its settings and connections.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have any issues.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience and for following the previous steps. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, restarted your phone, and still can’t send MMS, let’s check a few more possible causes:

1. Are you currently connected to Wi-Fi? Sometimes, MMS may not work properly if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled.
2. Do you know if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on in your phone’s settings?

If you’re not sure, please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled and, if it is, try turning it off. After that, attempt to send a picture message again.

Let me know if you need instructions on how to check or turn off Wi-Fi Calling, and please tell me your phone model if you do.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Is there something else I should look at or try?

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. Since we’ve checked mobile data, APN settings, and Wi-Fi Calling, the next step is to make sure your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS.

Could you please check if your messaging app has permission to access storage and SMS? If you’re not sure how to check or change app permissions, let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy), and I can guide you through the steps.

Once you’ve checked or updated the permissions, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, storage, phone.
